To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) even a drug test that is highly accurate by conventional measures (e.g., 99.9% accurate) can have an unacceptably high “false accusation” rate (that is, the test will identify many individuals who do not use drugs as drug users); and 2) a multi-stage Bayesian approach can be used to assure that a drug-testing procedure will have a low false accusation rate, and that the results of a Bayesian drug test will be credible evidence of drug usage
